title: Lesson 14 - Sandbox-to-Production Lifecycle: CLI, Change Sets, and Environment Parity
description: Manage the development lifecycle with available tooling, focused on provisioning Data 360 in sandboxes and promoting configuration with the CLI, change sets, and API based deployment.

questions.question: An admin created a Data 360 sandbox and the connections show Inactive with no data flowing. What is the correct next step?
options: Activate each connection and provide its authorization details
questions.explanation: Connections replicate without their stored credentials, so they arrive Inactive and must be activated with fresh authorization. Refreshing the sandbox is the strongest distractor and is wrong because a refresh does not carry credentials into the sandbox either.

questions.question: Which step must happen before the Data Cloud Setup menu becomes available in a new Data 360 sandbox?
options: Matching production licenses so the Data Cloud license syncs
questions.explanation: The sandbox inherits Data Cloud licenses from production, so Match Production Licenses must complete before the Data Cloud Setup menu is available. Publishing a data kit is wrong because it comes after the sandbox is provisioned and configured, not before.

questions.question: A team deploys a DevOps data kit with the Connect REST API and the request times out. What is the most likely fix?
options: Add more components to the kit
Deploy to a different data space
Set async mode so the deployment processes asynchronously
Remove the Data Cloud Architect permission set from the user
questions.explanation: The Connect REST API deploy is asynchronous, and omitting async mode can make the request time out before completion. Removing the permission set is the strongest distractor and is wrong because Data Cloud Architect is required for the deploy, not a cause of the timeout.
